statement: A membership-recovery read that reconstructs 'the set of members belonging to an already-frozen or historical generation' from a live, generation-blind table (no version/generation column, and no time boundary the code actually applies) must never be trusted as that generation's membership once new members can be written into the same table after the freeze. The read must be bounded by an explicit, verified generation/cohort marker — never merely 'whatever the shared table currently contains, filtered only by domain' — or it will silently re-absorb every subsequently-assigned member as if it were part of the original frozen snapshot.

FIX IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-05, per explicit operator direction (schema-level, option (1) of the two proposed here): `invariant_contexts` gained an explicit `crystal_generation_id text` column (migration supabase/migrations/20260930200000_invariant_contexts_crystal_generation.sql), valued with the ASSIGNING crystal-version artifact's own `research_objects.object_id` (e.g. 'EXP-P1/crystal-vP1') — never a freeform 'v1'/'v2' string, per the operator's own naming guidance. Backfilled mechanically: the 15 rows dated 2026-08-04 -> 'EXP-P1/crystal-vP1'; the 53 rows at the exact 2026-09-05T10:06:41.303889Z assignment timestamp -> 'EXP-P1/crystal-vP2' (also provisioned as a first-class `research_objects` row at `draft` lifecycle in the same migration, mirroring the existing crystal-version artifact model). `services/research/artifacts.ts::ensureCurrentCrystalGenerationId` resolves + idempotently provisions the CURRENT generation for every future Stage 8 assignment (app/api/research/crystal/[experimentId]/assign/route.ts's POST handler), so no future assignment can land untagged. `resolveFrozenPredecessorContext` now reads membership DIRECTLY via `listInvariants({domain, crystalGenerationId: frozenPredecessor.id})` — bounded to the frozen predecessor's own generation, never a re-derivation of 'whatever the domain currently contains'. `crystalFrozenManifest.ts`'s own domain-wide hash-verification read is UNCHANGED — it answers a different question (does the live corpus byte-reproduce the frozen hash) and was deliberately left untouched; legacy freeze semantics (`verifiedAgainstFreeze: false`, `legacyVerificationState: 'scientific-content-verified'` for the historical vP1 freeze) are unaffected by this repair, which touches only membership RECOVERY, never hash verification.
